lead: When everyone can build an agent, building turns into a price auction. The owner still doesn't know where to start, what is worth automating, where the risk is, or whether it worked. That is what the consultant delivers: clarity before the build and proof after it.
objetivo: explain why the diagnosis is worth more than the agent and write your own positioning statement as an AI consultant.

aprende.t: Why building got cheap and trust got expensive
The four boxes of a diagnosis: person, agent, simple automation, ceases to exist
What the consultant delivers and what they are not
Write your positioning statement in two lines

hero_alt: A workbench with tools pushed aside and, in the foreground, a clipboard with a checklist and a pen.

secoes.sub: The agent is the last piece. Click each block.

nos.detalhe: The owner arrives with a tool in mind, almost always seen in a video or at a competitor. The request is the starting point of the conversation, not the specification of the work.

Find the process that holds back the result, measure what it costs today (the baseline), and split the work into the four boxes: stays with the person, goes to an agent, stays simple automation, or ceases to exist.
From the opportunities found, pick one or two that deliver quick value and are feasible with the data and the team the company already has. Also say what NOT to do.
Test it for 30 days, with one team, one metric, and a stop criterion agreed on beforehand. If it doesn't work, switch it off with no harm done.

Compare against the baseline at 30, 60, and 90 days. This is where the consultant becomes a long-term partner: the model changes, the process changes, and someone needs to check that it's still worth it.

secoes.volta: What you measured at the end becomes the baseline for the next cycle
secoes.legenda: The builder comes in on the last step. The consultant answers for all five.

rolagem_fim.texto: Request, diagnosis, priority, pilot, and measured value. Without the diagnosis, the agent solves the wrong problem; without measurement, no one knows whether it helped.

secoes.titulo: What changes for people who work with AI
secoes.sub: Four ideas that underpin the program.

passos.sub: the price drops with every generation
texto: Models get cheaper and more capable every few months. In September 2026, Claude Opus 5.5 arrived costing 40% less than Opus 5 in typical use, according to Anthropic.
Anyone who only sells "I'll build your agent" is competing on price with a subscription the client can also sign up for.

exemplo.texto: The value moves away from "knowing how to do it" and toward knowing what to do, where the risk is, and whether it worked.

passos.sub: lots of interest, few agents in use
texto: In a 2026 Gartner survey of technology executives, only 17% of organizations already had AI agents in use, and more than 60% expected to have them within two years.
Between interest and real use there is a gap: choosing the process, preparing data, testing small, and measuring.

exemplo.texto: In the gap between "we want AI" and "we know AI helped."

texto: Every process you map comes out split into four: what stays with a person (judgment, relationships), what goes to an agent (a path that changes each time), what becomes simple automation (fixed rule), and what should stop existing.
The fourth box usually gives the cheapest win.

exemplo.texto: Overdue invoice reminder: simple automation. Answering a product question on WhatsApp: agent with limits. Approving a discount above the price list: person. A report nobody reads: stops existing.

texto: An AI consultant is not a security auditor, a lawyer, or a legacy-system programmer. When the case calls for a legal opinion, a penetration test, or heavy integration, you bring in someone qualified.
The INEMA certification in this program is a qualification, not a regulated profession. Tell the client this.

exemplo.texto: "I do the diagnosis, the prioritization, and the measurement. For formal LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) and security, I bring in a specialist."

secoes.sub: Copy it, replace what is between < >, and read it out loud.

blocos.conteudo:
I help <type of company> <result as a number or decision>
starting with a <time frame> diagnosis.
I don't <what you don't do: sell tools before the diagnosis,
program legacy systems, give legal opinions>.

I DO: discovery, diagnosis, prioritization, pilot plan, 30/60/90 measurement.
I DON'T: legal opinions, penetration tests, integration with legacy systems.
I CALL A SPECIALIST WHEN: <sensitive data at scale, contract, security>.
MY RESULT IS MEASURED BY: <client indicator against the baseline>.
MY CERTIFICATION: INEMA qualification (not a regulated profession).

blocos.rot: Prompt: stress test of the statement
blocos.conteudo:
You are the owner of a distribution company with 40 employees, skeptical about AI.
Read my positioning statement below and:
1) say in one line what you understood I sell;
2) ask the 3 toughest questions you would ask before hiring me;
3) point out any jargon word or promise you don't believe.
Don't compliment me.

Statement: <paste here>

abas.html:
I help distributors and wholesalers of up to 100 people to cut customer response time without growing the team, starting with a two-week diagnosis.

I don't sell tools before the diagnosis or program the company's management system.

• Naming a tool ("WhatsApp agent specialist"): the tool changes every quarter; the client's problem stays.
  • Promising a number ("I'll raise your sales by 30%"): you haven't measured anything yet.
  • Empty second line: someone who doesn't say what they don't do looks like they do everything.

secoes.sub: Two short exercises. Do them before moving on to lesson 2.

exercicios.texto: Fill in the two-line template. Run the stress-test prompt and rewrite until it finds no jargon or promises.
exercicios.pronto: the statement has two lines, names no tool, and the second line says what you don't do.

exercicios.texto: Fill in the five-line card and show the statement and the card to two people who don't work with AI.
exercicios.pronto: both people can repeat, in their own words, what you do and what you don't do.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Why is "I build your agent" a fragile position?
opcoes: Because agents don't work in SMBs.
Because building became cheap and the client compares it with the price of a subscription.
Because it's illegal to build agents without certification.
Because the client doesn't want agents.
perguntas.explica: Agents work, but building them has become a commodity. What stays scarce is knowing which process to change, the risk, and whether it worked. The common mistake is thinking the problem is technical.

perguntas.p: At Horizonte, which box does the automatic reminder for an overdue invoice go in?
perguntas.explica: It's a fixed rule: it's overdue, so send the reminder. It doesn't need a language model. Putting an agent here means paying more for something less predictable.

perguntas.p: The client asks for a legal opinion on whether their data use complies with LGPD (Brazil's data protection law). What do you do?
opcoes: You give the opinion, because you know the law.
You do the diagnosis and bring in a lawyer for the formal opinion.
You ask the agent to write the opinion.
perguntas.explica: You point out the risk in the diagnosis, but the legal opinion belongs to someone who is licensed to give it. This is in your scope card.

itens.texto: The owner buys clarity: where to start, what is worth doing, where the risk is, and whether it worked.
Person, agent, simple automation, and stops existing. The last one is usually the cheapest win.
Say what you don't do and when you bring in a specialist.
